따뜻하다.x: The weather is warm in spring.
따뜻하다.t: Also used for people: 따뜻한 사람 = a warm-hearted person. Pronounced [따뜨타다].

잠옷.x: As soon as I get home, I change into my pajamas.

명절.m: traditional holiday (such as Seollal or Chuseok)
명절.ex: 명절에는 고향에 가는 고속도로가 많이 막혀요.
명절.x: During the holidays, highways to people's hometowns get really jammed.
명절.e: Literally 'famous festival' — mainly 설날 and 추석.

챙기다.m: to pack, to take (with you), to remember to bring; to look after
챙기다.x: They say it'll rain. Make sure to take an umbrella.
챙기다.e: Also caring: 밥 잘 챙겨 먹어 = 'make sure you eat properly'.
챙기다.t: Hard to translate: it means making sure something or someone is taken care of.

이렇다.m: to be like this, to be this way
이렇다.ex: 이런 날씨에는 집에 있는 게 좋아요.
이렇다.x: In weather like this, it's better to stay home.
이렇다.e: Short for 이러하다, 'be this way'; part of the set 이렇다, 그렇다, 저렇다.

입금.m: deposit (of money), payment into an account
입금.ex: 입금이 확인되면 바로 물건을 보내 드릴게요.
입금.x: As soon as the payment is confirmed, we'll send the item.
입금.e: Literally 'money entering'; the opposite is 출금, 'money leaving.'
입금.t: Pronounced [입끔] — the ㄱ after ㅂ becomes tense.

양보.x: I gave my seat to an elderly woman on the subway.
양보.e: Literally 'yield a step' — stepping back so someone else goes first.
양보.t: 자리를 양보하다 (give up your seat) is the classic collocation.

확인.ex: 출발하기 전에 비행기 시간 확인을 꼭 하세요.
확인.x: Be sure to check your flight time before you leave.
확인.t: Pronounced [화긴] — the ㄱ batchim slides into the next vowel.

장단점.m: pros and cons, strengths and weaknesses
장단점.ex: 도시 생활과 시골 생활에는 각각 장단점이 있어요.
장단점.x: City life and country life each have their pros and cons.
장단점.e: Literally 'long and short points' — strengths and weaknesses.
장단점.t: Pronounced [장단쩜] — the ㅈ tenses in this compound.

악화되다.m: to get worse, to worsen, to deteriorate
악화되다.x: My cold got worse as the weather turned cold.
악화되다.t: Formal; in everyday speech, 나빠지다 is more natural. Pronounced [아콰되다].

충돌.ex: 두 사람은 의견 충돌이 자주 있어요.
충돌.x: The two of them often clash over their opinions.
충돌.e: Literally 'strike and rush' into each other.

급여.x: Our company's pay comes in on the 25th of every month.
급여.t: 급여 is the formal, paperwork word; in conversation people usually say 월급.

동호회.ex: 저는 주말마다 사진 동호회 사람들과 같이 사진을 찍으러 가요.
동호회.x: Every weekend I go out taking pictures with people from my photography club.
동호회.e: Literally 'a meeting of people who like the same thing.'
동호회.t: Use 동호회에 가입하다 for 'to join a club'; school clubs are usually called 동아리 instead.

형편.x: My family was struggling financially, so I worked part-time.
형편.e: 형 'shape' + 편 'convenience': the shape your life is in right now.
형편.t: 형편이 어렵다 is a polite, indirect way to say a family is poor.

마카롱.ex: 이 가게 마카롱은 크림이 정말 많아요.
마카롱.x: The macarons at this shop have tons of cream.
마카롱.t: Korea's thick, overfilled version is jokingly called 뚱카롱 (뚱뚱하다 'fat' + 마카롱).

워크숍.ex: 회사 워크숍 때문에 주말에 강원도에 가요.
워크숍.x: I'm going to Gangwon-do this weekend for a company retreat.
워크숍.e: From English 'workshop'; in Korean offices it often means an overnight team retreat, not just a class.
워크숍.t: Often spelled 워크샵 in daily writing, but 워크숍 is the standard spelling.

소외 계층.ex: 이 단체는 소외 계층 아이들에게 무료로 공부를 가르쳐요.
소외 계층.x: This organization teaches underprivileged children for free.
소외 계층.e: Literally 'social layers left on the outside'.

명예.ex: 그는 가족의 명예를 지키기 위해 노력했어요.
명예.x: He worked hard to protect his family's honor.
명예.e: Literally 'name and praise': a good name.
명예.t: 명예 훼손 'defamation' appears often in news about malicious online comments.

로켓.ex: 로켓이 큰 소리를 내며 하늘로 올라갔어요.
로켓.x: The rocket roared up into the sky.

고기압.ex: 고기압의 영향으로 내일은 전국이 대체로 맑겠습니다.
고기압.x: Thanks to high pressure, skies will be mostly clear nationwide tomorrow.

경유.ex: 이 비행기는 도쿄를 경유해서 뉴욕에 가요.
경유.x: This flight goes to New York via Tokyo.
경유.t: Use as 'A를 경유해서' = 'via A'; at gas stations, 경유 means diesel.

우르릉.forms: 우르릉 + 울리다 / 소리가 나다; 우르릉 쾅쾅
우르릉.x: Dark clouds gathered, and then thunder rumbled.
우르릉.e: 의성어 (sound word) for a deep, rolling rumble, like thunder or a heavy machine.
우르릉.t: Thunder in Korean picture books goes 우르릉 쾅쾅: the rumble, then the crack.

낙제.ex: 시험을 너무 못 봐서 낙제할까 봐 걱정돼요.
낙제.x: I did so badly on the test that I'm worried I'll fail.
낙제.e: Literally 'falling from the ranks' of those who passed.
낙제.t: Pronounced [낙쩨]; 낙제점 means a failing grade, also used figuratively.

풍자.ex: 이 소설은 당시 정치인들을 날카롭게 풍자하고 있어요.
풍자.x: This novel sharply satirizes the politicians of that time.
풍자.e: Literally 'mocking and piercing' — criticism that stings through humor.
풍자.t: Traditional 탈춤 mask dances are famous for 풍자 aimed at corrupt nobles (양반).

회의적.ex: 전문가들은 그 계획의 성공 가능성에 회의적입니다.
회의적.x: Experts are skeptical about the plan's chances of success.
회의적.t: Homonym alert: 회의 most often means 'meeting'; 회의적 always means skeptical, never 'meeting-related'.

실질적으로.ex: 이 정책은 서민들에게 실질적으로 도움이 됩니다.
실질적으로.x: This policy is of real, practical help to ordinary people.
실질적으로.e: Literally 'of real substance' — in actual effect.

보도국.ex: 방송사 보도국은 선거 날 밤새 바쁘게 일했어요.
보도국.x: The station's news department worked busily all night on election day.

환자식.x: Hospital meals are bland, but they're good for your health.

먹이 사슬.ex: 사람은 먹이 사슬의 맨 위에 있다고 해요.
먹이 사슬.x: They say humans are at the very top of the food chain.
먹이 사슬.e: 먹이 'feed' comes from 먹다 'to eat' + -이; 사슬 means 'chain.'

통탄하다.m: to deeply lament, to bitterly deplore
통탄하다.ex: 국민들은 어이없는 사고로 아이들을 잃은 것을 통탄했습니다.
통탄하다.x: The nation bitterly mourned losing children in such a senseless accident.
통탄하다.e: Literally 'painful sigh' — the strongest of the 'sigh' verbs.

인사청문회.x: The ministerial nominee's confirmation hearing was held at the National Assembly.
인사청문회.e: Literally 'personnel hearing' — lawmakers question a nominee before appointment.
인사청문회.t: 인사 here means personnel appointments, not its everyday sense of greeting.

경선.m: primary, party race (a competitive vote to pick a candidate or leader)
경선.ex: 당내 경선에서 이긴 후보가 대선에 나갑니다.
경선.x: The candidate who wins the party primary runs in the presidential election.

자기장.ex: 지구에는 나침반 바늘을 움직이는 자기장이 있어요.
자기장.x: The Earth has a magnetic field that moves a compass needle.
자기장.t: Don't confuse 자기 'magnetism' here with 자기 'oneself' — context makes it clear.

장단.m: rhythmic cycle (in Korean traditional music), beat; length (long and short)
장단.ex: 고수가 북으로 장단을 맞추면 소리꾼이 노래를 시작해요.
장단.x: When the drummer sets the rhythm on the drum, the singer begins.
장단.e: Literally 'long and short': the pattern of strong and weak beats.
장단.t: 장단을 맞추다 means to keep the beat, and figuratively to go along with someone.

흥건하다.x: After working out, my back is soaked with sweat.
흥건하다.t: Used with sweat, water, blood or tears: 땀이 흥건하다, 바닥에 물이 흥건하다.

오월동주.m: bitter enemies forced to cooperate, strange bedfellows
오월동주.ex: 두 경쟁 회사가 위기 앞에서 오월동주하는 상황이 되었습니다.
오월동주.x: The two rival companies ended up as uneasy allies in the face of the crisis.
오월동주.e: Literally 'Wu and Yue in the same boat' — two warring ancient states sharing one boat in a storm.
